Component origins

How a release reuses two separately authenticated original component archives.

About 3 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Rules 02 Signed macOS executor

A release can carry a component from an earlier published bundle. The bundle that supplies a component is its origin, and the origin is recorded per component.

flowchart LR
  A["SDK bundle 0.4.7<br/>--reuse-components-from + --components-sha256"] -->|gatewaySdk only| C["release stage<br/>package/release.json"]
  B["relay bundle 0.5.0<br/>--reuse-native-from + --native-sha256"] -->|native only| C
  D["this checkout<br/>fresh build"] -->|runtime, scripts, JavaScript| C

package/release.json keeps the legacy top-level bundleVersion / bundleSha256, which name the reused SDK bundle when present, otherwise the reused relay bundle. Each component also has its own origin, so the relay can point at a separate archive:

{ "reusedComponents": { "bundleVersion": "0.4.7", "bundleSha256": "…",
  "components": {
    "gatewaySdk": { "buildVersion": "0.4.7", "sourceSha256": "…",
      "origin": { "bundleVersion": "0.4.7", "bundleSha256": "…" }, "files": [] },
    "native": { "buildVersion": "0.5.0", "sourceSha256": "…",
      "origin": { "bundleVersion": "0.5.0", "bundleSha256": "…" }, "files": [] } } } }

Rules

  • Each archive is authenticated on its own: whole-archive SHA-256, safe tar entries, the complete checksum manifest, the six component files, its own upstream pins, release profile, source digest, and (for the gateway SDK) its capability. The native binary bytes are authenticated by the whole-archive checksum and the complete manifest; the relay's original receipt carries no binarySha256 field, so only the SDK's receipt hash is additionally checked against its archived binary. Only the named component paths are taken from it; two origins can never supply the same path.
  • An archive that already reused the selected component is refused. Reuse the bundle that built it, so the receipt's bytes stay the original's.
  • --reuse-native-from requires --native-sha256, both --with-native and --with-gateway-sdk. Without the SDK reuse pair, the SDK must pass the normal fresh-build checks. With --reuse-components-from and --components-sha256, each component comes from its independently authenticated original archive. Native reuse excludes --fresh-native.
  • Runtime resolution (src/gateway-sdk-runtime.ts): a component origin that is complete and valid wins; a missing origin falls back to the parent receipt, so releases built before this field still verify. A present but partial or malformed origin fails closed, with no fallback.
  • Receipts and binaries are copied byte for byte. Re-copied files are re-hashed against the verified digest before they reach the stage.

Signed macOS executor

Managed macOS installations prefer the signed gateway SDK inside the app when its signed receipt identifies the exact original executor and Code Mode companion in the selected CLI release. The app and helper must pass Developer ID and fixed identifier checks, and the signed package is verified before and after signature validation. The executor path is stable across app releases; its Developer ID identity allows macOS to recognize Keychain access grants across updates. The original CLI checksum remains the compatibility identity exchanged by clients and the service. A missing, changed or mismatched app falls back to the verified CLI executor, preserving CLI-only installations and release-skew behavior.

This does not prove that Keychain will retain an existing grant: confirm an approval on the signed executor and check a later restart and app update on the unlocked Mac. macOS can ask again for other credentials or changed access rules. For unattended MCP OAuth operations, see MCP credential storage.
